items.title: SUBMITTED 2026-09-05: Zomby Woof s412162 revision r8902998, pending moderation. VERIFIED FROM SONGSTERR'S OWN DATA: 115 bars (rebar landed), 1573 drum notes, kick lane35=0 lane36=348 (lane merge landed), staccato 32 and ties 5 preserved. TWO OF FOUR ITEMS LANDED. Kick-on-one-lane: YES. Bar 2 rebarred 10/16 into 5/16+5/16: YES. TOM SPACING: NO, the importer ignored it. I moved Low Tom StaffLine 5->6 and Very Low Tom 6->8 on the drumkit articulations, and the live revision still reads Mid Tom at staff pos 2, Low Tom 2.5, Very Low 3, identical to before. GHOST NOTES: not attempted, <Ghost> appears zero times in the GPIF so it is not expressible in the file. GENERAL RULE NOW PROVEN: Songsterr's importer takes note events, lanes, bars, meters, rhythms and ties from the file, and IGNORES the instrument and per-note layer, keeping its own drumkit articulation StaffLines, track names and note flags. So tom spacing, track names and ghost notes ALL need the editor, not an import. EDITOR IS THE BLOCKER: its controlled inputs reject every scripted value route (five tried on the track name, plus the submit textarea), and keystrokes stopped landing partway through this session even with focus confirmed on the element.

ZOMBY WOOF GHOST/LETRING AUDIT, PARTIAL, 2026-09-05. ESTABLISHED: (1) letRing is ZERO in every GPIF source, grep count 0 for LetRing/letRing/let-ring, so the project's zero-letRing requirement is already met and there is nothing to remove. (2) The automatic transcription r7115188 carries exactly 32 ghost detections at known positions, extracted to s412162/audit/ghost-letring-audit.json with bar, voice, slot, lane, staff position: bars 4(5), 13(6), 15(5), 40(4), 41(4), 42(4), 43(4). (3) 22 of the 32 sit on hi-hat lanes, 18 closed HH and 4 pedal HH. (4) The live tab carries 32 stray STACCATO marks on those same notes, put there by r8787022, which is wrong notation for a ghost and is the confusing marking in that passage. (5) Drumnet's chart of bar 4 read at 8x shows five quintuplet groups with accents on group starts and PLAIN noteheads, no brackets. NOT ESTABLISHED, do not ship a verdict without it: whether Bedard or Ryan Brown show parenthesised noteheads at the specific 32 positions. Bedard's handwriting at 5x resolves the apparent parentheses into stems and beam strokes; a higher-resolution scan or a different source is needed. Brandon's rule stands: parentheses in a real transcription ARE genuine audio ghosts, so the verdict must come from a readable source. MY TWO ERRORS THIS PASS: I generalised an all-32-false verdict from one bar of one chart, and I printed ASSERTION PASSED on a PyGuitarPro round trip that contained 0 notes and 0 measures, a vacuous gate. The GP5 builder needs fixing before any validation claim. ALSO: PyGuitarPro has native NoteEffect.ghostNote and letRing (both default False) but CANNOT read GP7 .gp, so any PyGuitarPro path requires building the model from the GPIF.

ZOMBY WOOF GHOST AUDIT, CORRECTED 2026-09-05. I WAS WRONG: I read Drumnet bar 4, saw no brackets, and generalised an all-32-false verdict across seven bars. Brandon corrected it and I verified at 30x: Drumnet p1 DOES print parenthesised snare noteheads, clearly visible in the repeated figure of its bars 6-8 as thin curved arcs flanking the filled noteheads, distinct from the thick straight stems. He also identifies them in its bar 5 after the open hi-hat. Those are genuine soft ghost strokes and must be PRESERVED. POLICY CHANGE FROM BRANDON: do NOT delete notes for missing transients, quiet strokes can be masked in a recording. BLOCKER, THE REAL ONE: Drumnet bar numbers do not map to tab bar numbers past bar 5. Tab meters read 3/4 10/16 2/4 5/4 then FOUR bars of 15/16; Drumnet reads 3/4 10/16 2/4 5/4 then ONE 15/16 then 4/4. Ryan Brown's chart also has 15/16 x4 per the earlier session, so Drumnet is the outlier and may be using a repeat or omitting bars. Until that alignment is settled the printed ghosts cannot be matched to the 32 detections at tab bars 4, 13, 15, 40-43. NEXT: establish the Drumnet-to-tab bar map by matching content, not numbers, then assign ghostNote=True at the matched positions. Zero letRing is independently satisfied, 0 occurrences in every GPIF source. Crops at s412162/audit/drumnet-zoom/ and bedard-zoom/.

ZOMBY WOOF GHOSTS MAPPED 2026-09-05, alignment solved. SECOND CORRECTION: my claim that Drumnet has only ONE 15/16 bar was wrong. I misread the courtesy 4/4 at the right edge of system 3 as bar 6's meter. Drumnet system 2 ends at bar 5; bars 6,7,8 inherit 15/16; 4/4 starts at bar 9. Tab and Drumnet bar numbers DO align, which matches Ryan Brown's 15/16 x4. THE MAPPING: tab bars 5-8 are four repeats of one figure with HH open at slot 4 and a snare pair at slots 6 and 7. Brandon located the ghosts as 'measure five immediately after the open hi-hat strike' and 'the repeated figures across measures six through eight'. That is exactly slots 6 and 7 in bars 5,6,7,8, and it matches the two adjacent parenthesised noteheads verified at 30x in the Drumnet crop. RESULT: 8 GENUINE GHOST NOTES, snare, bars 5/6/7/8 at slots 6 and 7, to be set ghostNote=True with reduced velocity. ZERO overlap with the 32 automatic detections at bars 4,13,15,40-43, so the transcriber MISSED every printed ghost and invented 32 elsewhere, 22 of them on hi-hat lanes where ghost brackets are not valid notation. REMAINING: apply ghostNote=True at those 8 positions, keep letRing at 0 (already satisfied), and decide what to do with the 32 stray staccato marks r8787022 left on those same wrong notes.

GHOSTS SUBMITTED 2026-09-05 as r8903886, VERIFIED LANDED, plus a regression I introduced earlier. GHOSTS: 8 ghost notes confirmed in the live revision data, all snare MIDI 38, bars 6/7/8/9 at slots 6 and 7 exactly as audited. That is the parenthesised snare pair Drumnet prints immediately after the open hi-hat in the repeated 15/16 figure. GPIF element is <AntiAccent>Normal</AntiAccent>, grounded across 20+ Zappa .gp files; searching for <Ghost> returns zero and is the WRONG element name, which is why I earlier reported ghosts absent from the file layer. LETRING: zero in source and output, verified; requirement met and independent. TECHNIQUE NOTE: ghosting required copy-on-write at the BEAT level, not just the Note. My first attempt edited a shared Note and produced 32 renderings across bars 6,7,8,9,48,50,52,54 instead of 8; the verifier caught it. Cloning the Beat per target slot keeps it bar-local. REGRESSION I CAUSED: staccato went 32 -> 129 at r8903141, the TOMS revision, not at the ghost revision. My uploaded files contain ZERO <Staccato> elements, so Songsterr added 97 marks itself when the 99 Low Tom notes moved from lane 45 to lane 43. r8903886 carries them forward. This is the same class as the track names: Songsterr's per-note flag layer acts independently of the file. NEXT: find whether staccato can be cleared from the file side the way AntiAccent can be set, since ghost proved the flag layer IS writable from the .gp.

CORRECTION: THE 97 EXTRA MARKS ARE MY BUG, NOT SONGSTERR'S. I earlier queued that Songsterr added 97 staccato marks on import. Wrong. Root cause: kickfix_generic.py maps a source note onto a target note keyed ONLY on (String, tie role). It ignores every other effect child. When I moved the 99 Low Tom notes from lane 45 to lane 43, they all mapped onto Note 788, which carries <Accent>1</Accent>. So 99 notes gained an articulation marking they never had, and the live data shows VeryLowTom staccato going 2 -> 101 while LowTom went 2 -> 0. THE RULE, same family as the String collision bug: a lane merge must map each source note onto a target with an IDENTICAL EFFECT SET, not just the same String and tie role. Effect children seen on drum notes in this file: Accent, AntiAccent, Tie. FIX NEEDED in kickfix_generic.py: build the match key from (String, tie role, sorted list of effect child tags and values) and create a new Note when no exact match exists, exactly as apply_ghosts.py now does. AFFECTED REVISIONS: r8903141 and r8903886 both carry the 99 wrongly-accented tom notes. r8902998 does not. If a moderator approves either of the later two, those 99 notes ship with a marking the source never had.

OPEN HI-HAT QUESTION RESOLVED 2026-09-05, and a new accent gap found. Ryan Brown's DRUM Magazine page (1178x733, nearly 2x Drumnet's width) read at 6x shows bar 1 as 3/4, eighth=178, 0:00, with THREE circled-x noteheads on the top space, each carrying an accent wedge. Circled-x IS Brown's open hi-hat glyph and it is exactly what Songsterr renders. So Songsterr's three HHopen at bar 1 slots 3, 6, 8 are CORRECT and match Brown one for one. The earlier 'three against one printed circle' concern came from Drumnet using an X plus a separate open-circle symbol, a different convention, not from Songsterr being wrong. NEW DEFECT FOUND: Brown accents all three open hi-hats in bar 1. Songsterr bar 1 has ZERO accents. So the missing-accent problem is not confined to the 5/4 fill; bar 1 needs 3 accents added at slots 3, 6 and 8 on the HHopen notes. STILL UNRESOLVED: the foot hi-hat. Brown's bar 1 shows small downward wedge marks below the staff under the kick stems at roughly x=1180 and x=1560 in the 6x crop, which could be foot hi-hat or could be stem terminations; needs a tighter crop to settle. The grace note before the 5/4 fill also remains unchecked against Brown. Crops at s412162/audit/brown-zoom/.

ACCENTS ARE EXPRESSIBLE ON SONGSTERR DRUM STAVES, corrected 2026-09-05 by Brandon ('i see the accent option'). Two sessions had wrongly agreed there is no accent field. FIELD IS `accentuated`: 1=accent, 2=marcato, present on drum staves live (Keep It Greasey s604777 Vinnie Colaiuta 60 at value 2; Drowning Witch s620961 drums 7 at 1 and 2 at 2). GPIF <Accent> IS A BITFIELD not an enum: 1=staccato(bit0), 4=accent(bit2), 8=marcato(bit3), 9=8|1. Verified against Drowning Witch GPIF {1:246, 4:4, 9:4, 8:3}. So writing <Accent>1</Accent> correctly yields a staccato; use 4 or 8 for accents.
